title: How is the number of originals lodged back for a Bill of Lading correction reconciled?
content:
## Scope

This rule of the Bills of Lading and Transport Documents product fixes the number of original documents written on a lodgement, when the originals of an issued transport document are handed back to the line at the origin office so that a requested correction of the printed document can go ahead.

## Formal clause

1. The number of originals written on the lodgement is reconciled from the whole documentation history of the document. It is never taken from the caller's own count.
2. The reconciled number is the sum of the originals counted on every originals-issued entry of the document, less the sum of the originals counted on every originals-surrendered entry, less the sum of the originals counted on every originals-voided entry, and it is never less than zero.
3. Because an earlier set is always fully returned or voided before the next set is issued, this whole-history balance is exactly the number of originals of the set in force still in circulation.

## The same clause as input, treatment and output

| Read from the documentation history of the document | Treatment in the balance |
|---|---|
| Originals counted on every originals-issued entry, whichever set | Added together |
| Originals counted on every originals-surrendered entry | Taken away |
| Originals counted on every originals-voided entry | Taken away |
| A balance that would fall below zero | Recorded as zero |
| A number of originals the caller states or believes it holds | Not used |

## Hypothetical worked cases

The histories below are invented for illustration; they are not company figures.

- **Case A.** One originals-issued entry of 4 originals, no surrender, no void. The balance is 4 less 0 less 0, so 4 originals are written on the lodgement.
- **Case B.** Set 1 issued with 4 originals, all 4 later surrendered, set 2 issued with 4 originals. Issued entries total 8, surrendered entries total 4, voided entries total 0; the balance is 8 less 4 less 0, which is 4, and these are the originals of set 2, the set in force.
- **Case C.** One originals-issued entry of 4 originals and one earlier lodgement recorded as 3 originals surrendered. The balance is 4 less 3, so 1 original is written.
- **Case D.** An inconsistent history in which issued entries total 2, surrendered entries total 2 and voided entries total 1. The arithmetic would fall below zero, so the balance is recorded as zero.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** the caller says it holds two originals, so two is written. **Correct basis:** the history balance governs; the caller's own count is never used.
- **Wrong reading:** only the entries of the current set are added up. **Correct basis:** every entry in the whole history of the document is summed; the balance equals the set in force only because earlier sets are always fully returned or voided before a new set is issued.
